To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pQCD prediction of $\Upsilon(2S)\to\ell\ell$ leptonic decay rate is more accurate after applying the PMC, which is based on the RG-invariance, and that the RG-improved pCQ prediction agrees well with experimental data.
the PMC has been successfully applied to the $\Upsilon(2S)\to \mu^+\mu^-$ decay and the $\Upsilon (1S)\to e^+e^-$ decay.
the RG-improved pCQD prediction for $\Upty(1S)\rightarrow \mu^+\mu^-$ agrees well with experimental data, and it is the first time that the PMC has been applied to a bottomonium decay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pQCD calculation of the $\Upsilon(3S)$ leptonic width.
the application of the principle of maximum-conformality (PMC) in the pQCD calculations for the $\Upsilon(2S)$ and $\Upsilon(3S)$ leptonic decays.
the pQCD prediction of the $\Upsilon( 1 S)$ leptonic decay width.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PMC has been applied to the $\Upsilon(2S)$ leptonic width [6] and the $\Upsilon (3S)$ leptonic and hadronic widths [7] in a similar manner.
our RG-improved pQMCD prediction is more convergent, more accurate and consistent than other pQCD predictions.
our RG-improved pQC prediction is consistent with experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PMC can be applied to any QCD observables, including the leptonic decay of heavy quarkonium states.
the PMC can be used to improve the pQCD predictions for $\Upsilon(nS)\to \mu^+ \mu^-$ decay rate.
the PMC provides a systematical and reliable way to solve the pQCD renormalization scheme ambiguity, which is a long standing issue in pQCD calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PMC provides a systematic and rigorous method for improving perturbative predictions in QCD and other gauge theories.
PMC is a powerful tool for pQCD predictions.

the PMC is a systematic method to resum the $\beta$-function terms and to determine the optimal renormalization scale at any perturbative order, and thus to achieve a more convergently pQCD series and more accurate pQMCD predictions.
